observations: body L1-L8: the dashes before «Hinc» and «Manifeste» measure 9.7 and 10.4 pt; «al–Battānī» (L2) is letter-spaced, with a long dash (5.4 pt). The degree sign of «11° 45′» in L7 prints as a filled dot. Rule I is al-Battānī's p. 87, L5-L8 (the distance between the settings of the Sun and the Moon in degrees of the settings) and p. 87, L32-L33 (the Moon visible when it equals or exceeds the arc).

body L9-L16: rule II is p. 87, L14-L17: the excess or defect of the elongation over 12° 11′ taken in proportion to 12° 11′, the «portio» by which the arc of visibility 11° 45′ is decreased or increased (p. 87, L19-L21, L29). A speck prints under the S of «Si» (L9).

body L17-L29: rule III is p. 87, L17-L31, with the third column of the table of correction (Part II, p. 89; see note 2 and p. 267, note 1): 30 minutes the mean distance, and the twelfth part by which the apparent diameter of the Moon grows and diminishes (p. 87, L23-L24). Al-Battānī's lunar diameters of p. 236, 29′ 30″, 32′ 25″ and 35′ 20″, differ from the mean by 2′ 55″, 1/11,1 of it, his «fere duodecima parte». A speck prints over the u of «nuetur» (L23). The bars of the formulas (L23, L24) are a minus sign and the fraction bars.
body L30-L34: a mark prints over the e of «est» (L31). The dash before «Schiaparelli» measures 10.4 pt; a heavy bracket closes Schiaparelli's addition begun on p. 266, L22.

body L35-L38: «Al–Farghānī», «93–96», «al–Ǵaghmīnī», «256–57» and «150,v.–151,v.» have long dashes (5.3 to 5.9 pt), the dash before «Ḥabash» measures 8.3 pt. Al-Farghānī's 12° of the equator pass in 48 minutes of time; the Moon gains 12° on the Sun in about a day, «nychthemero fere».

notes_left L1-L6: the elongation as the hypotenuse of a right triangle with the latitude and the difference in longitude as its sides is al-Battānī's rule of p. 87, L9-L11; p. 87, L11-L13 refers to the more exact precepts of chapter XXVI. «al-Battānī» (L5) is letter-spaced, with a hyphen (2.6 pt); the c of «ceptis» (L6) prints as a filled blot.

notes_right L1-L7: the Sūrya-Siddhānta, chapter X, treats the rising and setting of the Moon; the Pañcasiddhāntikā is Thibaut and Sudhākara Dvivedī's edition cited on p. 206, note 2. A nāḍikā is the sixtieth part of a day, 24 minutes, so 2 nāḍikā are 48 minutes of time, in which 12° of the equator pass. «Indi» and «Burgess-Whitney» are letter-spaced; «Sūrya-Siddhānta», «Burgess-Whitney» and «1-3» have hyphens (3.1 to 3.4 pt).
